title: zlib compressed data format (RFC 1950)
summary: zlib wraps a DEFLATE stream with a 2-byte header (CMF + FLG) and a 4-byte Adler-32 trailer. The header encodes the compression method (always 8 = DEFLATE), window size, and flags. The FLG byte's high 4 bits must make (CMF*256 + FLG) a multiple of 31.

ext.summary: zlib wraps a DEFLATE stream with a 2-byte header (CMF + FLG) and a 4-byte Adler-32 trailer. The header encodes the compression method (always 8 = DEFLATE), window size, and flags. The FLG byte's high 4 bits must make (CMF*256 + FLG) a multiple of 31.

structure.meaning: Compression Method and Flags: low 4 bits = CM (8 = DEFLATE), high 4 bits = CINFO (log2(window size) - 8, so 7 = 32KB window).
Flags: bits 0-4 = FCHECK (makes CMF*256+FLG divisible by 31), bit 5 = FDICT (preset dictionary), bits 6-7 = FLEVEL (compression level).
Present only if FDICT is set; Adler-32 of the preset dictionary.
Adler-32 checksum of the uncompressed data (big-endian).

ext.example_decoded: zlib header (CMF=0x78 DEFLATE/32KB, FLG=0x9C) + empty stored block + Adler-32 of empty (0x00000001)
notes: zlib is used by HTTP (Content-Encoding: deflate), PNG (IDAT uses zlib), PDF, and many protocols.
Adler-32 is faster than CRC-32 but less robust for error detection.
Preset dictionaries (FDICT) improve compression for small, similar messages.
